messages:
alexa: FYI I'm drafting a calibration dataset + prompt set for the upcoming FP8/INT8/GPTQ/AWQ bakeoff. Need quick alignment on scope and sampling.
raj: high level: represent production traffic distribution + stress edge cases. size tiers: tiny (2k), medium (10k), large (50k) — agreed? :+1:
sam: also include structured vs unstructured inputs (code, json, tables). quantization seems to break numeric precision in code paths.
maria: we should stratify by token length (<=32, 33-128, 129-512, >512) and by intent (qa, summarization, instruction, dialogue, code). ensures kernel selection sees realistic seq-lens.
eve: for GPTQ/AWQ we need activations — so the calibration set must include batched forward passes that match batch/seq distributions (and the same tokenizer).
raj: good point. add explicit note: use same tokenizer/config as serving. no subword mismatch.
alexa: prompt templates — default: zero-shot instruction, 3-shot in-context, chain-of-thought (when allowed), and a rerank pair for embeddings tests. Include stop sequences too.
sam: include a small curated adversarial set for hallucination/regression detection: ambiguous queries, math, dates, and prompt injection patterns.
maria: metrics proposal: exact-match for code snippets, EM/ROUGE for summarization, BLEU for translation, embedding cosine for semantic similarity, plus logits-based metrics: KL divergence, rank-correlation (Spearman) between FP32 logits and quantized logits.
eve: add "logits-MSE on top-k" and token-level top-1 accuracy delta. we saw that helps surface subtle calibration drift.
raj: calibration data selection strategy: 60% in-distribution, 25% long-tail (rare intents/domains), 15% adversarial/edge. random seed + stratified sampling for reproducibility.
alexa: sample script idea for reproducible draws:
```
python tools/sample_calib.py --source s3://datasets/traffic-2025 --n 10000 --stratify intent,length --ratios 0.6,0.25,0.15 --seed 42 --out calib-10k.jsonl
```
sam: add metadata per example: original_source, domain_tag, token_count, and prompt_template_id. helps debugging when metrics spike.
maria: for prompt curation, we should canonicalize templates and keep 10 variants per template (verbatim, concise, verbose, mention instructions explicitly, role play) so quantization doesn't overfit to one phrasing.
alexa: agree. also include non-English sample (es, fr, de, zh) at ~5% to catch tokenizer/char-embedding regressions.
eve: benchmark harness notes: run each quant config 3 seeds, measure mean+std. capture latency and memory too (deployment profile matters).
raj: deployment profiles to exercise: low-latency (seq<=128, batch=1), high-throughput (seq=256, batch=8), long-context (seq=2048+), and on-prem constrained (1 GPU, mixed workloads).
sam: we should record per-layer activation histograms during calibration runs — helps diagnose which layers lose dynamic range under INT8/AWQ.
maria: for AWQ/GPTQ param choices: try per-channel vs per-tensor; symmetric vs asymmetric; and with/without outlier clipping. track which combinations yield <1% EM delta for critical tasks.
alexa: reporting: per-model table: metric deltas vs FP32, latency delta, memory footprint, and recommended deployment profile. include short notes on whether fine-tuning quant-aware or calibration-only fixes regression.
eve: CI note: add a job that runs the tiny (2k) calibration + eval on PRs that touch quant code. ci-bot: queued job quant-calib-quick on runner-2, will post results as comment. :robot_face:
raj: action items: (1) sam to write sample selection script, (2) maria to author prompt templates + variants, (3) alexa to define metrics dashboard layout, (4) eve to add activation capture hooks. target: draft calib-10k + eval harness by EOW.
sam: on it. I'll ping when draft script lands in tools/.
maria: I'll create a spreadsheet with templates and example items per variant.
alexa: sweet. one more: document the "no-syntactic-filtering" rule — don't strip markdown/code blocks during sampling; we want fidelity to traffic.
eve: and preserve original whitespace/escape sequences — tokenizer edge cases often hide there.
raj: ok team, let's keep iterations tight. we'll start with medium set and iterate to 50k if needed. :rocket:
